meta.title: Rebuilders Anonymous, Week 4
meta.data_note: Every number in this issue is real. Fantasy points come from the league on Sleeper, box-score lines from Sleeper’s Week 4 NFL stats, and game context from ESPN’s recaps, all pulled on October 8. The pulled data is saved next to this issue in newsletter/issues/2026-week4/.

lead.headline: Micah won with a quarterback who took one snap
lead.dek: Case Keenum handed off once for the Bears and sat down. Micah parsons fan club won by 29.58 anyway, because the other ten starters had a week.

stats.label: Snap played by Micah’s Superflex, Case Keenum, out of Chicago’s 93
Micah’s winning margin over Skat’s BruteForce Theorem anyway
Targets T.J. Hockenson caught, for 119 yards

body: Micah parsons fan club played Week 4 with ten working starters and won by 29.58. The eleventh was Case Keenum at Superflex. According to ESPN, Keenum lined up under center for Chicago’s first play against the Jets, pitched to D’Andre Swift for 2 yards, and then Tyson Bagent took over at quarterback for the rest of the game. Keenum’s line for the week is 1 snap and 0.0 points.

Keenum was a reasonable pickup. Micah added him on September 30, after he started Chicago’s Monday night win over Philadelphia and threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns, and started him in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield out with a dislocated thumb. To make room, Micah dropped Keon Coleman. Coleman caught 6 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown for Buffalo on Sunday, including a 34-yard score from Josh Allen.

The rest of the lineup made it a non-event. Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in Dallas’s 34-30 win in Houston, all in the second half and a career high, for 31.3. Hockenson caught every ball thrown to him in Minnesota’s 15-10 win over Miami (24.9). Zay Flowers had 8 catches for 118 yards and a touchdown (25.8), and Jake Bates made all four of his field goals for 18.0.

Even the other quarterback got hurt. Lamar Jackson left Baltimore’s win over Tennessee with an ankle injury after 33 of 64 snaps and still scored 18.88 on 15-of-20 passing for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Micah has since claimed Bagent for $0, dropped Keenum, and added Tyler Huntley, who went 8 of 9 in relief of Jackson. Micah is 3-1 with the sixth-most points in the league and $10 of FAAB left.

rankings_intro: The order is our opinion. Records, scores, and points for are facts.

rankings.take: Lost by 39.16 and still has 89.56 more points than anyone else this season. Kenneth Walker ran for 177 yards at Las Vegas. The problem is next week, when Mahomes, Walker, Young, and Hubbard are all on bye.
The week high and the second-most points of the season. Dak Side has also given up 614.90, the most in the league, which is how the second-best team is 2-2.
Tied for the best record with the sixth-most points. Won this week with a Superflex who took one snap. Has spent $190 of $200, so the next quarterback emergency gets solved for $10 or less.
Two straight wins after an 0-2 start. CeeDee Lamb and Nico Collins played against each other in Houston and combined for 72.1 points for the same fantasy team.

Tetairoa McMillan scored 45.2, more than the 39.84-point margin by himself. The bench had another 74.0, including Emanuel Wilson’s two touchdowns for Seattle. Then PB paid $5 for Keon Coleman, the best claim of the week.

Fourth in points and suddenly hurt. Tee Higgins left with a groin injury after 157 yards and Saquon Barkley lasted 4 snaps. The answer was $70 on Will Shipley, the Eagles back who ran 6 times for 23 yards.
Third in points for the season, held back by the quarterbacks. Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants and Daniel Jones scored 7.92. The two of them combined for 18.36.
Benched the best quarterback score in the league and lost by 13.72. Traded for Ladd McConkey and Rico Dowdle on Tuesday. New players help more when the right ones start.
Won with the second-lowest score of the week. Matthew Stafford threw for 317 yards and no touchdowns, Marcus Mariota lasted 10 snaps, and 78.22 points sat on the bench.
Alvin Kamara, a free pickup on September 30, scored his first two touchdowns of the season. Big Shough has the fewest points of any 2-2 team and the best free-agent add of the month.
Fewest points in the league, and now officially rebuilding. On Sunday morning Skat’s traded Emeka Egbuka for two 2027 second-round picks, then dropped Tyreek Hill for George Holani 24 minutes later.
The week low, on a lineup that had two different ways to win on the bench. Brian Robinson scored three touchdowns while sitting. Caleb Williams has now missed two straight games.

recaps.headline: One snap from Keenum, and it still wasn’t close
recaps.body: Skat’s got a real game from Kyle Monangai, who carried 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns as Chicago wore down the Jets, and Carnell Tate caught 9 passes for 145 yards for Tennessee. It wasn’t enough against a team playing a man short. Skat’s bench scored 3.0 in total, the lowest in the league, so there was no better lineup sitting there. Skat’s lost to Javonte Williams’s three touchdowns and a tight end who caught 13 of 13.

w_keys.line: 19 car, 62 rush yds, 3 TD; 5 rec, 21 yds

recaps.headline: UC benched the best quarterback day in the league
recaps.body: Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes in New England’s 29-26 win at Buffalo, the last one with 1:50 left, and ran for 54 yards. That was 26.16 points, the best quarterback score of the week, from Unsportsmanlike Conduct’s bench. Jalen Hurts started instead and went 12 of 27 for 93 yards in a loss to the Rams (13.52). DeVonta Smith started at receiver and has no stats for the week. Maye for Hurts and Quentin Johnston’s 5.0 for Smith adds 17.64 to a team that lost by 13.72. Big Shough won on Alvin Kamara’s first two touchdowns of the season.

recaps.headline: Kyren Williams takes the last four minutes and the week high
recaps.body: Split Safety scored 160.36, the fifth-best total of the week, and lost by 39. Kyren Williams ran for two touchdowns in the final four minutes of the Rams’ comeback in Philadelphia and caught 10 passes on top of that. Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards in a loss to Jacksonville, and Chase Brown caught 11 of his passes. Split Safety lost Ja’Marr Chase to a concussion in the second quarter of that same game after 15 snaps. It also started a kicker who attempted no field goals (2.0) with Cameron Dicker’s 12.0 on the bench.

recaps.headline: McMillan catches 14 and the whole margin
recaps.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 of 16 targets for a career-high 192 yards and both of Bryce Young’s touchdown passes in Carolina’s 32-26 win over Detroit. ESPN noted he finished one catch and nine yards short of the franchise records. Take his 45.2 away and ThePeopleBeaters lose. Mendoza’s quarterback problem showed up in New York, where Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions in Arizona’s 36-24 loss. The Giants quarterback who beat him, Jameis Winston, threw three touchdowns from ThePeopleBeaters’ bench.

l_keys.line: 13 car, 47 rush yds, 1 TD; 3 rec, 27 yds

recaps.headline: CeeDee Lamb catches 17 and the last word
recaps.body: CeeDee Lamb caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards and scored the winning touchdown with 40 seconds left in Houston. On the other side of that game, Nico Collins came back from two missed games with a hamstring injury and caught 7 for 118 yards and two scores. hammball started both and got 72.1 points out of one box score. J’Allen got 26.7 from Tee Higgins, who had 157 receiving yards before a groin injury in the fourth quarter, and 19.0 from Will Reichard’s five field goals. Saquon Barkley hurt his hamstring after 4 snaps and scored 2.0.

recaps.headline: Same game, wrong running back
recaps.body: Rams of Steel had a running back on each side of Monday night’s Falcons-Saints game and started the one on the losing side. Kendre Miller, picked up on October 1, ran 6 times for 9 yards and lost a fumble for New Orleans (1.9). Brian Robinson ran for three touchdowns in Atlanta’s 45-24 win, from the Rams’ bench (25.7). That one swap is worth 23.8 in a 16.2-point loss. Kingslayers won with the second-lowest score of the week, thanks to Puka Nacua’s 125 receiving yards and a rushing touchdown in his first game back after missing two.

w_keys.line: 23 car, 73 rush yds, 1 TD against his old team

awards.name: Manager of the Week
awards.body: Week high by 10.62. Seven starters scored at least 18, and the lowest of them was Dak Prescott, who threw for 335 yards in Houston.

awards.name: Lineup Crime
awards.body: Started Kendre Miller (6 carries, 9 yards, a lost fumble) over Brian Robinson (three touchdowns) in the same game. Deebo Samuel’s 18.0 on the bench would also have flipped it. Two separate ways to win, both sitting.

awards.name: Best Performance in a Loss
awards.body: 177 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City’s 30-27 win at Las Vegas, including the go-ahead run with 3:21 left. Next Gen Stats had him at 21.21 mph on a 76-yard run. He still got caught from behind.

awards.name: Shortest Shift
awards.winner: Case Keenum, Micah parsons fan club
awards.body: One handoff, then the bench. Runner-up is Marcus Mariota of the Kingslayers, who started for Washington in place of an injured Jayden Daniels, left after the second drive with a knee injury, and scored 5.34 on 10 snaps. Both of their fantasy teams won.

awards.name: Bench of the Week
awards.body: The most points left on any bench, including Romeo Doubs’s two touchdowns for Green Bay and 11.42 from Jalon Daniels, the undrafted rookie who started for Tampa Bay. Kingslayers won anyway, so nobody has to talk about it.

transactions.summary: The Wednesday waiver run processed 7 claims for $101, and $70 of it was J’Allen buying the next Eagles running back. The best claim cost $5: ThePeopleBeaters got Keon Coleman, the receiver Micah dropped for Keenum, a few days after his 116-yard game. Two trades went through, both involving teams under .500, and Skat’s added a third rebuilding move by spending $14 on Thursday for a Chiefs running back in the Chiefs’ bye week.

trades.teams: Skat’s BruteForce Theorem and WELL! It's The Big Shough
trades.summary: Big Shough got Emeka Egbuka, Kaelon Black, and Skat’s 2027 third-round pick. Skat’s got Jadarian Price, Antonio Williams, and two 2027 second-round picks, Dak Side’s and Big Shough’s own.
trades.note: The trade went through at 12:22 p.m. Eastern. Big Shough started Egbuka 38 minutes later and got 2 catches for 13 yards. Price is on injured reserve. For a 1-3 team, two second-round picks is the right direction.

trades.teams: Rams of Steel and Unsportsmanlike Conduct
